**Tier G** — governance — identity, capability, delegation, audit · owned by `platform` · `public.password_reset_requests`

**One row is** One "Forgot password?" request for one account, from the moment the person asks until a super admin resets the password or dismisses the request (PLAN.md §4 D251).

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | `super_admin` |
| Write capability | `super_admin` |
| Minimum project role | `viewer` |
| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | **none** |

RLS on, NO policy and no table grant: which accounts asked for a reset is not one PostgREST query away. The one writer for a NEW row is `request_password_reset(p_email)`, callable by anyone signed out — it records a row only for an ACTIVE account, at most one open per account, and answers identically in every case so it cannot be used to discover which emails exist; it writes an access-plane `auth.password_reset_requested` audit row naming the account as TARGET and no actor, because whoever typed the email is not proven to be its holder. A request changes nothing about the account. Super admins list open requests through `admin_list_password_reset_requests`, close one as `dismissed` through `admin_dismiss_password_reset_request`, and `admin_reset_user_password` closes the account's open request as `resolved`; both write an `admin_audit_logs` row. The super admin's identity is client-asserted (§4 D28).

> **RLS is on and this table has no policy.** That is deny-all for every role except
> `service_role`, which bypasses RLS. If a page reads this table directly and gets zero
> rows, this is why.

| `status` | — | `text` | — | — | `open` until a super admin acts; then `resolved` (the password was reset) or `dismissed` (the request was not genuine, or was handled another way). CHECK-constrained, and `closed_at` is set exactly when the status is not `open`. |

| `closed_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When a super admin resolved or dismissed the request; NULL while it is open. |
| `closed_by` | — | `uuid` | — | — | The super admin who closed it; NULL while open, or once that account is deleted (`ON DELETE SET NULL`). |
